extracted.intended_audience: USPTO leadership, employees, policymakers, and external stakeholders (inventors, practitioners, partner organizations)
extracted.subtask_description: Agency-level performance, human capital, outreach, financial, and program standards and metrics used by the USPTO to evaluate and run workforce development, recruitment, education, regional-office, and funding activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: All-employee People Survey (diagnostic items/dimensions)
rubrics_metrics.description: This year’s survey included 63 diagnostic items across 14 different dimensions and allowed employees to provide open-ended comments to questions. Questions also helped evaluate the employee value proposition and perceptions of women in STEM positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used annually (vs. FEVS sample); response rate reported (61%); overall employee engagement score reported (74%). Findings identified core strengths (customer focus, immediate supervisors, culture of accountability). Results were discussed in off-site meetings with executive management and union leaders to inform action planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employee engagement score & core strengths
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall employee engagement score and identification of core strengths and areas for improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example metrics: 74% engagement score; use dimension-level analysis to identify declining scores vs. favorable areas; preserve and leverage core strengths such as customer focus, immediate supervisors, and culture of accountability when planning interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: After Work Education (AWE) Program eligibility and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: AWE is a voluntary program available to eligible employees to develop and enhance work skills related to the agency’s mission by taking classes at an accredited college or university.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courses should improve current performance, expand/enhance current job, or enable employees to develop skills/knowledge for other agency positions. Continued funding reflects agency value on educational opportunities and career advancement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Upward Mobility Program (UMP) requirements & outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides career development for employees in positions/series with limited advancement; eligible employees apply for trainee positions and an Individual Training Plan (ITP) is developed for selected employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upon successful completion of an ITP, employees may be reassigned or non-competitively promoted to the corresponding target position—i.e., program is a pathway to non-competitive promotion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative Professionals Excellence (APEX) Program structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Nine-month voluntary program for Technical and Administrative Support Staff employees at the GS-5 through GS-12 levels with a comprehensive curriculum to enhance professional career and personal growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Learning activities include live classroom discussions, core and elective self-paced computer-based training modules, a mid-year review, and conclusion with a capstone project. Participants have networking opportunities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leadership Forum participation & training requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Bi-annual four-day Leadership Forum offering keynotes and workshops on topics attendees indicated were important; managers were required to attend 12 hours of training over the four days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program uses pre-Forum surveys to set workshop topics, mixes internal and external speakers, provides webcast access for remote workforce, and tracks participation (example: of 1,170 eligible leaders invited, 1,040 participated in at least one session).

rubrics_metrics.name: SES Leadership Academy (LA) objectives and pilot
rubrics_metrics.description: Cohort-based leadership development program for incumbent Senior Executive Service (SES) intended to achieve individual interpersonal and enterprise excellence; design based on research and industry studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pilot cohort planned for Feb 2017. FY2016 included administration of 360 leadership assessments to all USPTO SES members with subsequent coaching to interpret results and update executive development plans.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervisor Certificate Program (SCP) and Leadership Development Program (LDP) scope
rubrics_metrics.description: SCP addresses leadership competencies for supervisors (managing self, people, and projects) tailored to new USPTO supervisors; LDP provides leadership training across individual, aspiring, mid-, and senior-level leaders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SCP offered cohorts and piloted virtual instructor-led training (vILT) to reach teleworkers and regional office staff; LDP enrollment and cohort summaries are tracked (enrollment figures provided in report charts).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hiring targets and mission-critical hires
rubrics_metrics.description: FY2016 hiring targets included 474 mission critical hires (patent examiners, administrative patent judges, trademark examining attorneys, information technology, HR specialists, contract specialists, general attorneys).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track actual hires to goal by business unit and job class (figures and charts provided). Use targeted outreach and hiring fairs to meet mission-critical staffing needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Veteran hiring goals
rubrics_metrics.description: Veteran hiring goals for FY2016: 10 percent for patent examiners and 20 percent for non-patent examiner hires.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Veterans Hiring Program (VHP) conducts local and regional events, partners with universities and military associations, and tracks resumes received (example: 450 resumes received). Use veteran-targeted outreach to meet percentage goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital recruitment & social media strategies
rubrics_metrics.description: Use integrated and interactive digital recruitment strategies (LinkedIn, Twitter, Facebook, YouTube) and content categories (e.g., ‘Job of the Week’, ‘Job Spotlight’) to engage candidates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of activities: first recruitment Twitter chat, LinkedIn premium content categories, careers site redesign. Track social metrics (example: LinkedIn followers exceeded 20,000, a 113% increase in two years).

rubrics_metrics.name: Careers website redesign and digital outreach best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Redesigned USPTO Careers website to provide an improved user experience with rich targeted content and imagery that can be easily accessed and shared.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Engage stakeholders and user communities to ensure accuracy and usability; measure site engagement and repeat visits as recruitment indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recruitment messaging, partnerships, and targeted brochures
rubrics_metrics.description: Development of brochures and messaging to promote hiring authorities (e.g., Schedule A for disability hiring), and targeted outreach to specific demographics and institutions (Hispanic Serving Institutions, HBCU/TCU events).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As part of site redesign, create dedicated sections for disability hiring and other special placement programs; collaborate with federal and educational partners to widen candidate pipelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law School Clinic Certification Program participation standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Program enables law school students in participating clinics to prepare and prosecute patent and trademark applications under the guidance of an approved faculty clinic supervisor and program guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final Rule effective June 27, 2016 (Public Law 113-227). Track program outputs: during first three quarters of FY2016, participating schools filed 107 patent applications and 465 trademark applications; program expansion measured by participating schools (43 participating law schools).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Pro Bono Program availability & expansion
rubrics_metrics.description: Provides free legal assistance to under-resourced inventors and small businesses to secure patent protection; expanded to support nationwide availability via service providers and state-level launches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monitor establishment of pro bono service providers and state program launches to measure geographic and capacity expansion.

rubrics_metrics.name: STEM education & outreach integration with IP
rubrics_metrics.description: Office of Education and Outreach (OEO) provides programming for students, educators, and young inventors to integrate STEM knowledge with IP concepts; builds partnerships to expand reach and relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program examples: NSTI teacher institute, Thingamajig Invention Convention expansion, FIRST Global Innovation Award collaboration, JamTech programming, Universal IP Patch development, Science of Innovation video series. Metrics include program sites, participation counts, and content produced (videos and lesson plans).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee structure philosophy and objectives
rubrics_metrics.description: Fee structure philosophy objectives: Promote Administration Innovation Strategies; Align fees with the full cost of products and services; Set fees to facilitate effective administration of the patent and trademark systems; Offer application-processing options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conduct comprehensive biennial fee reviews consistent with philosophy; share proposals with public advisory committees (PPAC/TPAC), hold public hearings, analyze comments, and publish NPRMs and final rules as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of public advisory committees & rulemaking process for fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Develop fee proposals, present to PPAC/TPAC, conduct public hearings, receive comments, revise proposals, issue NPRMs, and publish final rules after analysis of comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: trademark NPRM May 27, 2016; final rule Oct 21, 2016; patent fee NPRM Oct 3, 2016 with plan to publish final rule in Summer 2017. Track number and substance of comments received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial Advisory Board role and deliverables
rubrics_metrics.description: A formal Financial Advisory Board reviews and analyzes data and proposals impacting fee collections and spending and provides recommendations to USPTO executives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Board recommendations cover financial risk management, spending priorities, fee-adjustment proposals, and size of operating reserves needed to mitigate financial and operational risk.

rubrics_metrics.name: Operating reserve policy & minimum balances
rubrics_metrics.description: Formal operating reserve policy to manage two operating reserves within acceptable balance ranges with a minimal balance target set for two years and a longer-term optimal balance objective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Minimum balances (example values): $300 million for Patent Business Line and $55 million for Trademark Business Line. Minimums are reviewed annually and set to mitigate known financial risks to core operations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle of balancing revenue increases with cost-efficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: While aligning revenue with program costs is critical, the USPTO cannot simply raise fee rates to pay for every desired improvement; the agency must focus equally on revenue and spending sides.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maximize cost-efficiency and transparency; when reserves risk dropping to low levels, undertake holistic review of spending priorities to identify critical investments and rein in non-essential spending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional office establishment and roles
rubrics_metrics.description: Establish regional offices (Detroit, Denver, San Jose, Dallas) to support mission by offering services, engaging communities, and facilitating hiring and retention of a diverse nationwide workforce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track regional activities: outreach events, seminars, Patent Quality roundtables, PTAB hearings, AIA trial proceedings, and educational competitions. Monitor staffing levels (example totals and per-office PTAB judges and patent examiners) and local engagement metrics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regional office staffing and activity metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Staffing counts and activity outcomes for each regional office (examples: Texas—first class of examiners, five new PTAB judges; Silicon Valley—50 utility and 11 design examiners, 23 PTAB judges; Rocky Mountain—17 PTAB judges and 62 patent examiners; Midwest—10 PTAB judges and 116 patent examiners).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these staffing and activity numbers to demonstrate regional capacity to deliver examination, PTAB hearings, outreach events, and community engagement; report events and program-firsts (first live IPR, first AIA trial, patent drafting competitions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Labor-management forum and collaborative pilots
rubrics_metrics.description: Labor Management Forum (LMF) aims to enhance labor-management relationships and promote measurable improvements; LMF develops processes for outage response and amends policies on work schedule notification, communication, and collaboration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: LMF negotiated agency-wide pilot initiatives (Office of the Ombudsman Pilot and the Innovation Challenge) launched in FY2016. Use LMF to surface employee-inspired solutions and pilot innovations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affinity groups engagement and OEEOD partnership activities
rubrics_metrics.description: Network of 16 voluntary employee affinity groups led by volunteers to host cultural, social, and career-development programs; OEEOD partners with affinity groups to host programs promoting cultural understanding and creates on-demand videos for remote workforce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track events (e.g., International Food Sample Festival, special emphasis month events), video production and reach, and support for unique celebrations (Lunar New Year, Diwali, Eid, Nowruz, Walk of Thankful Recognition).
